sections.body: Artificial intelligence in economics and investing now means specific computational work across ten areas. Macroeconomic econometrics and quantitative trading use machine learning on time series, order books, and price data to forecast and execute. Private equity, fixed income, and portfolio construction apply models to screen companies, score credit risk, and allocate capital under constraints. Reading the market's language and alternative data turn filings, news, satellite images, and transaction records into tradable signals. Agent workflows chain models to automate reconciliation, reporting, and routine analysis, while crypto and governance systems monitor on-chain activity and fiduciary checks.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of the field is uneven. Macroeconomic forecasting has improved nowcasts but still fails at turning points, and quantitative trading suffers from crowding and overfitting. Credit scoring is mature for consumer loans, while corporate default models remain unreliable in rare stress events. Portfolio construction has solved the mathematics of optimization, but the real limit is estimation error in expected returns. Language models can parse sentiment yet still hallucinate and miss negation, and alternative data signals decay quickly as more funds use them. Agent workflows are not trustworthy for unsupervised high-stakes decisions, crypto models face manipulation and thin liquidity, and governance tools flag obvious conflicts but cannot resolve ambiguous fiduciary duties.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for forecasting methods would start with Macroeconomic Econometrics, which covers the models behind growth and inflation projections. Quantitative Trading and Portfolio Construction sit next to each other, one for signal generation and execution, the other for allocation and risk budgeting. Private Equity and Deal Sourcing and Fixed Income and Credit Risk apply similar screening and scoring ideas to company acquisition and debt markets. Reading the Market's Language and Alternative Data are the two input pipelines, one for text and one for non-traditional datasets, feeding the trading and credit pages. Agent Workflows in Finance shows how these models are chained into operational tasks, while Crypto Markets and Decentralised Finance applies the same methods to on-chain data and liquidity pools. Governance and Fiduciary Risk sits across all of them, covering the legal duties and compliance checks that constrain what an AI system may do with client money.
